To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the K L → μ + ν μ decay is dominated by a vector form factor with a mass m V = (905 ± 17) MeV and that the scalar contribution is negligible.
the form factors of K 0 ( μ 3 ) decay are described by a linear and a quadratic term for the vector form factor, with a linear term only for the scalar form.

we measured the linear slopes of the vector and scalar form factors of K 0 L → π ± e ∓ ν e and K 0 L ( S ) → π ± μ ± ν μ decays to be λ + = 26.7 ( 0.6 ) × 10 - 3 and λ 1 = 11.7 ( 1.0 ) × 10-3, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for the Higgs boson and the study of its properties, as well as the search for new particles predicted in various theories.
the study of K0(mu+mu-) and K0(mu3)-decays.
the study of the form factor of the K 0 → π μ ν decay.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NA48 experiment has performed a precise measurement of the K L form factors, which is consistent with previous results and which is the most precise to date.
the NA48 data is in good agreement with the predictions of the Standard Model.
our data do not support the presence of a scalar pole.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the K 0 ( μ 3 ) resonance is a vector state, and its mass is 905 ± 17 MeV / c.
we have measured the K 0 → μ 3 form factors with unprecedented accuracy.
we improved the measurement of the form factor parameters by about a factor 3 and 4 respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the form factors are well described by the pole model with a vector pole mass m V = 905 MeV/c 2.
the form factors of K L → π + μ − ν μ decay have been measured to a high level of precision.
the form factors are consistent with a simple pole model.
